title: Damaged Surface with Roughness Variation Map
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that renders an interactive damaged surface material editor with procedural roughness variation mapping.

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (0x1a1a2e). Perspective camera at position (0, 2, 5) looking at origin.
- Add an OrbitControls for camera rotation (import from CDN).
- Three lights: one DirectionalLight (white, intensity 1.5) at (5, 8, 5), one PointLight (warm white 0xffeedd, intensity 1.0) at (-3, 3, -2), and one AmbientLight (0x404060, intensity 0.3).
- Render at full window size with antialiasing enabled. Use tone mapping (ACESFilmic) and set outputColorSpace to SRGBColorSpace.

## Main Object
- Create a large flat plane (PlaneGeometry, 6x6, 256x256 segments) rotated to face the camera at a slight angle (rotate X by -Math.PI/3). This represents the damaged surface.
- Use MeshStandardMaterial with:
  - Base color: 0x8B7355 (weathered stone)
  - metalness: 0.1
  - roughness: 0.5 (base, will be modulated)

## Procedural Roughness Variation Map
- Generate a 512x512 canvas-based roughness texture procedurally using layered noise:
  - Use a simple value noise function (seeded pseudo-random with interpolation).
  - Layer 1 (base wear): large-scale noise (frequency ~4), amplitude 0.4
  - Layer 2 (scratches): high-frequency directional noise (frequency ~32), amplitude 0.25
  - Layer 3 (impact craters): randomly place 5-10 circular regions of high roughness (value 0.9-1.0) with radius 10-30 pixels, with smooth falloff edges.
- Apply this canvas as the roughnessMap on the material.
- Also generate a matching bump map from the same noise data (darker = lower) and apply as bumpMap with bumpScale 0.15.

## Damage Painting System
- The user can paint additional damage onto the surface by clicking and dragging on the plane.
- Use a Raycaster to find UV coordinates of intersection with the plane.
- When painting, increase roughness values in a circular brush area (radius controlled by UI) on the roughness canvas texture.
- Each paint stroke adds roughness by 0.15 (clamped to 1.0). Mark the texture as needsUpdate after each stroke.
- Track total number of paint strokes applied and total damaged pixel count.

## UI Controls (DOM overlay)
- A panel in the top-left with:
  1. A slider labeled 'Brush Size' (range 5-50, default 15) that controls the paint brush radius in pixels.
  2. A slider labeled 'Base Roughness' (range 0.0-1.0, step 0.05, default 0.5) that adjusts the material's base roughness property.
  3. A slider labeled 'Bump Scale' (range 0.0-0.5, step 0.01, default 0.15) that adjusts bumpScale.
  4. A button labeled 'Reset Surface' that regenerates the original procedural roughness map, clearing all painted damage.
  5. A button labeled 'Toggle Wireframe' that toggles wireframe rendering on/off.
  6. A dropdown labeled 'Damage Preset' with options: 'None', 'Light Wear', 'Heavy Erosion', 'Battle Scarred'. Selecting a preset regenerates the roughness map with different noise parameters:
     - None: uniform roughness 0.3
     - Light Wear: base noise only, amplitude 0.2
     - Heavy Erosion: all layers, amplitude doubled
     - Battle Scarred: extra craters (15-20), scratch amplitude 0.5
- A HUD in the top-right showing:
  - 'Strokes: N' (number of paint strokes)
  - 'Damaged Pixels: N' (count of pixels with roughness > 0.75)
  - 'Avg Roughness: X.XX' (average roughness value across the entire map)

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields, updated every frame:
- cameraPosition: {x, y, z} rounded to 2 decimals
- baseRoughness: current material roughness value (number)
- bumpScale: current bumpScale value (number)
- brushSize: current brush radius (number)
- wireframeEnabled: boolean
- strokeCount: total paint strokes applied (number)
- damagedPixelCount: number of pixels in roughness map with value > 0.75
- avgRoughness: average roughness across all pixels, rounded to 4 decimals
- activePreset: string name of current preset
- craterCount: number of craters in current generation
- textureResolution: 512 (constant)
- materialMetalness: current metalness value
- lightCount: 3 (constant)
- surfaceSegments: 256 (constant)
- roughnessMapApplied: boolean (true if roughnessMap is set on material)
- bumpMapApplied: boolean (true if bumpMap is set on material)
- lastPaintUV: {u, v} of last paint position or null if never painted

## Animation
- Animate the point light in a slow circular orbit (radius 3, speed 0.5 rad/s) around the Y axis at height 3 to show how roughness variation interacts with changing light direction.
- Update state every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Roughness values must be clamped [0.0, 1.0]. Bump scale must be clamped [0.0, 0.5]. Brush painting must only affect pixels within brush radius. Average roughness must be mathematically consistent with pixel data. Damaged pixel count must accurately reflect pixels > 0.75 threshold. Reset must fully restore original procedural state. Preset changes must be deterministic and reproducible.
